answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. The rule makes a swarm of raven-like sockpuppets costly: an attacker must fund every identity and risks losing the funds, while honest agents can earn them back through valid work. Raising the stake for high-impact actions creates an onyx barrier without pretending identity is impossible; at the zenith, the cost scales with the influence sought.
